prompt: Do a picky engineering review of the latest commit (HEAD) in the Chibi checkout at /Users/cwaldner/Personal/chibi/.worktrees/review-eval/chibi. It adds a call-site census in Chibi and a typed element count in C. Read only, don't change anything. Save the review as review.md.
assertions: The review flags assert(matches++ <= array->count) in pin_array_count_type as a bug because the assert has a side effect that changes the returned count in debug builds.
The review flags the 'if (!array) return 0;' guard in pin_array_count_type as a silent guard on a state only a bug produces, recommending an assert or removal rather than keeping it.
The review flags the per-element xstrdup/free inside the pin_array_count_type loop as needless allocation.
The review flags comparing forest[index].kind against the string "call_expression" inside the per-node loop in CollectCalls.

The review flags LineOf/ColumnOf rescanning the text from the start for every call site (quadratic work) or notes that SnapshotNode already stores row and column, so line/column are duplicated or derivable.
The review flags CountCallsInForest as a wrapper that only forwards to CollectCalls and should be deleted.
The review flags the is_dead bool on CallSite (filtered by LiveSites, set by MarkDead) as list membership encoded in a flag, or flags MarkDead's sites-by-removed nested loop.
The review flags that the commit adds no test (no @test and no C test case) for the new behavior.
The review flags that the new procedures or the new C function have no callers in the repository (speculative or dead code).
Every reported finding gives concrete evidence (a count, measurement, named consumer/caller, or failing input) rather than only restating a rule.
The review does not recommend adding defensive NULL checks, fallback values or extra validation for internal invariants.
The review does not recommend splitting any function purely because of its length.
